name: hcapp_submitTrackImport
description: Registers an uploaded track file (GPX/TCX/FIT or a Strava/Garmin zip) as an HC.TrackImport job for the caller (E5.F5.S7). The bytes are already in blob storage (container track-imports, uploaded with a SAS from GetTrackImportUploadToken, which minted @jobId). Idempotent on @jobId. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 96, @param NULL); no permission gate — the job is always the caller's. The ProcessTrackImport function then does the work in slices the app drives, with a timer backstop.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Minted by GetTrackImportUploadToken; names the blob. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

parameters.name: blobUrl
parameters.description: The uploaded blob. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Every failure — auth, 1296 missing jobId (NULL or all-zero) or empty blobUrl (errorType 12), 1996 unhandled (errorType 19) — returns this, followed by the detail at index 1.
Follows ErrorEnvelope: errorId, errorType, errorCode, errorTitle, errorUserMessage, errorProc. No debugMessage column.

rowsets.name: Success
rowsets.description: success = 1. Note: only ONE column — no errorCode / errorType.

rowsets.name: Job
rowsets.description: On success: the job id (the existing one when resubmitted).

sideEffects: INSERT HC.TrackImport (id = @jobId, HasherId = caller, FileName = LEFT(@fileName, 250), BlobUrl, ByteSize); Status defaults to 0. Guarded by NOT EXISTS ... WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK) in a transaction, so resubmitting the same @jobId is a no-op success.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 1296 and in the CATCH (after ROLLBACK).

codeSmells.detail: These parameters have no SQL default, so a call that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs (unlogged empty 500): @deviceId, @accessToken. On 2026-10-13 every parameter whose body already handled NULL (and every sync watermark) was given a default; these remain because they are the auth pair or the body never checks them for NULL.

codeSmells.issue: Resubmitting another hasher's jobId reports success
codeSmells.detail: Line 76 checks only id = @jobId, not HasherId; a caller that sends someone else's job id gets success and that id back without a row of their own. jobIds are server-minted GUIDs, so this is a correctness wrinkle rather than an exposure.
Lines 62/87 use errorType 12 (missing parameter) and 19 (unhandled) rather than the standard 2 and 5.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
